<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary below to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
The summary doesn't state your years of experience, and there are no dates to calculate them from. **How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?**

**What it costs not to supply it:** The posting asks for 8 years as a hard requirement. Recruiters and applicant-tracking systems usually screen on that number first. A summary without it can't show you meet the bar, and many screeners will assume you don't and move on. I won't invent a figure, so without it the best I can do is emphasize scope and scale, which is weaker against a stated years requirement.

Here's a draft with a placeholder for the number:

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and operated a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Prior work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems, with consistent focus on correctness and reliability in high-volume backend environments.

**Once you give me the number:**
- **8 or more:** I'll put it first so it matches the requirement directly.
- **Under 8:** I'll rework the summary to lead with the depth and scale of your work (e.g., the 40,000 orders/day pipeline) rather than the number itself. It's also worth deciding whether to apply anyway, since the requirement may be flexible.
